speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision. Can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned and whether you are able to move it or bear weight on it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning, as severe groin pain with abnormal leg positioning after high-impact trauma is a classic sign of a hip fracture or dislocation. Can you tell me if your right leg appears shorter than the left, or is it rotated outward?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presentation of a shortened, internally rotated, and adducted leg is highly characteristic of a posterior hip dislocation. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray
